title: ÆTHER: Storm Entry v6 (one piece: storm, piano hook, tabla drums, hype finale)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

request.prompt: A brand-new mass hero ENTRY film score, ONE continuous piece built on ONE hero hook from the first second to the last, written the way today's biggest Tamil and Telugu film composers score the hero's first appearance. Exactly 112 BPM, C minor with a sharp-four F-sharp for menace, a whistle-able 5-note hero hook with Carnatic gamakam slides; every section uses THIS SAME hook, varied and growing, never a new tune. Instruments: a concert grand piano playing the hook in bold octaves is the signature voice; a real tabla, thavil, mridangam and kanjira played close, natural and dry; a natural nadaswaram; a gritty bent synth lead; a warm synth bass; deep wordless male crowd chants. 0-12 s: one thunder crack, rain ticking on a tin roof, the gritty synth plays a rising 3-note call (C, E-flat, G, bent up), the synth bass creeps in, the piano quietly hints the hook's first notes. 12-20 s: tension: the hook hinted low, a deep crowd hum rising. 20-30 s: the piano hook takes over in bold octaves, twice, carrying the transition; at 24 s one thunder boom and full band hit with a crowd 'HEY!' lands under the piano. After 26 s no more thunder or rain. 30-42 s: the tabla starts the groove under the same piano hook, then thavil, mridangam and kanjira join one by one; the nadaswaram answers the piano with the same hook. 42-55 s: a tabla and thavil call-and-response showcase, crowd claps and chants on the accents, the piano punctuating with short stabs of the hook. 55-62 s: the hook comes back hotter: thavil doubles time, crowd shouts 'HEY!' on every bar, piano and nadaswaram in unison, a fast tabla roll, then one beat of full band silence. 62-72 s: SLAM: the same hook lifted up a whole step, the biggest moment, piano octaves, nadaswaram and synth lead together over the full drums, crowd chant on every accent. 72-80 s: a korvai, one rhythmic phrase played three times by the whole band, landing on one massive final hit with a crowd roar, then the piano alone plays the 3-note call and lets it ring. Loud, punchy, clean, wide mix where the piano and drums are clearly heard. Not Western trailer music, not EDM, no side-chain pumping, no white-noise risers, no filter sweeps, no fade-out.

brief.notes: Jithesh 30 Oct 12:35: the stitched versions don't match (first 30 s vs after 30 s, and the end; the piano layer sat in the wrong places). v6 = everything he liked (storm opening, tabla-led drums, piano hook at 20-30 s and after, hype ending) written into ONE generation on ONE hook. No stitching or layering. 3 takes.

story: The storm brings the hero in, a piano hook carries his reveal, the festival drummers play for him and the festival explodes.
